tools.name: analyze_migration
tools.description: Analyze a PostgreSQL migration SQL for safety issues. Returns violations, risk level, and lock analysis.

tools.name: suggest_fix
tools.description: Auto-fix safe violations in a PostgreSQL migration SQL. Returns the fixed SQL and list of changes.

tools.name: explain_lock
tools.description: Explain what PostgreSQL lock a DDL statement acquires and its impact.

sql.description: A single DDL statement to analyze

tools.name: list_rules
tools.description: List all available MigrationPilot safety rules with descriptions.

tools.name: check_before_apply
tools.description: Safety gate: call this BEFORE writing or executing any PostgreSQL DDL or migration. Resolves the project's own MigrationPilot config (rule toggles, severity overrides, failOn threshold) exactly like the CLI, then returns a pass/fail verdict. On "fail", do not apply the migration — fix the blocking violations and check again.

sql.description: The exact SQL that is about to be written or executed

pgVersion.description: Target PostgreSQL version. Defaults to the config's pgVersion, or 17.

configPath.description: Path to a config file, or a directory to resolve config from. Defaults to searching upward from the working directory, exactly like the CLI.

tools.name: analyze_migration_dir
tools.description: Analyze every migration file in a directory. Returns per-file results plus an aggregate summary. Use this to audit a whole migrations folder before a release, or to find which existing migration introduced a risky pattern.

pattern.description: Glob pattern for SQL files, relative to path (default: **/*.sql, or the config's migrationPath)

pgVersion.description: Target PostgreSQL version. Defaults to the config's pgVersion, or 17.

tools.name: get_rule
tools.description: Get the full documentation for one MigrationPilot rule: what it reports, why it matters, whether it can be auto-fixed, and how to configure it. Call this when a violation ID appears and you need the reasoning behind it before rewriting a migration.

sql.description: Optional SQL to run this one rule against. When the rule fires, the response carries the exact violation message and the concrete safe alternative for that statement.
